data.title: Restore per-sub-PR LLM review + provenance-narrowed integration review + chunked oversized-PR fallback + merge-pipeline guards

content.text: After story 20d7-09d6-b831-4c3a deleted .github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml (epic b575), the project's PR/review workflow has degraded in compounding ways. The DSO maintainer running /dso:sprint and /dso:debug-everything fights a manual battle for every epic merge: ci.yml:llm-review is gated base_ref == 'main' so PRs whose base is a session branch receive no internal LLM review. Session-to-main reviews fail closed on cumulative diffs above ~6000 lines (LLM returns non-JSON, schema correction exhausts). Multiple workflows (ci-python-skills.yml, portability-smoke.yml, mirror-defenses-to-pr, 6+ others to audit) silently skip sub-PRs. .test-index RED markers can reach main. Version-bump commits land directly on main outside the PR (breaks subsequent git pull origin main). Worktree cleanup closes active PRs mid-CI. Three downstream epics (cf7b-86a9, f27a-3c6a, fb32-215c) are blocked.

- SC1 — Per-sub-PR LLM review + provenance-narrowed integration review + re-keyed cycle ledger and DefenseStore. Every per-story PR (sprint) and per-batch PR (debug-everything) triggers an internal LLM review via a new .github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml workflow. The branches: filter targets the PR's BASE branch matching session/**, session-**, session_**, bug-batch/** (story PRs are pushed FROM story/... TO session branch; batch PRs are pushed FROM bug-batch/... to session or main — base-ref filter is the correct primitive). The cycle ledger AND DefenseStore are both keyed by (pr_number, commit_sha); migration contract specifies v1.1.0-to-v1.2.0 sentinel-pr_number rule for existing entries (old commit_sha-only entries match against any pr_number until the next review cycle re-keys them); a contract test reads a v1.1.0 entry and asserts no data loss in v1.2.0 emission. Integration review at session-to-main (ci.yml:llm-review) reuses the existing verify-session-provenance.sh logic: exit 0 → skip LLM dispatch with explicit covered-by-sub-PR-reviews liveness assertion (check-run conclusion skipped + summary message listing covered sub-PR numbers and SHAs); exit 1 (unprovenanced) or exit 2 (budget-exhausted) → keep current full-diff path. A contract test ships with this epic locking the verifier's 0/1/2 exit-code semantics. Verification: the epic's own sprint demonstrates per-story sub-PR review firing AND a synthetic test exercises a 6000+ line all-provenanced session-to-main PR that completes without LLM dispatch.

- SC2 — Runner gracefully degrades on oversized PRs via pre-filter + file-level chunking + LLM aggregation pass + visibility trailer. Pre-filter uses .gitattributes linguist tags (linguist-generated, linguist-vendored, linguist-documentation) PLUS additive configurable ignore.glob / ignore.regex overrides. ignore.glob ships with a non-empty default value (lockfile patterns at minimum: **/package-lock.json, **/yarn.lock, **/poetry.lock, **/go.sum); both max_files and max_calls validate non-zero at config load with a warning on zero. File-level chunking EXTENDS the existing per-directory region-split (Strategy E in region_split.py) with finer-grain per-file dispatch for oversized single-file or single-directory clusters, preserving the file-atomicity invariant (single file is NEVER split across reviewers). An LLM aggregation pass synthesizes cross-file findings before posting. The aggregated PR comment includes a visibility trailer listing every file reviewed and every file skipped with skip reason. A hard upper bound max_files × max_calls routes to admin/FP-recovery via a distinct OVER_BOUND status (NOT FP-suspected) — /dso:fp-recovery rejects PRs with OVER_BOUND status, preserving FP-recovery's signal integrity. Verification: synthetic 7000+ line direct PR with mixed reviewable/ignored files produces aggregated findings with visibility trailer; the LLM never receives the full diff; a 200-file synthetic PR routes to admin/FP-recovery without silent passing.

- SC3 — Every CI gate on path to main fires per (PR, SHA); cross-workflow check naming is consistent. All workflows currently gated base_ref=='main' or pull_request: branches: [main] are audited; their pull_request branch filters are EXTENDED (additive, not narrowed) to cover session/**, session-**, session_**, bug-batch/** base refs OR an always-runs umbrella job is added so the required-check name remains stable across branches that may skip the conditional inner job. Behavioral test test-no-duplicate-checks-per-sha.sh queries the GitHub Actions runs API, groups workflow_run entries by (head_sha, check_suite_id), selects the entry with the highest run_attempt, and asserts uniqueness of check-context names across those latest-attempt entries (re-runs after failure are out-of-scope). Verification: behavioral test passes against a fixture run of the epic's own sprint; RED state on a duplicate-check fixture fails as expected.

- SC4 — Merge pipeline correctness — RED tests blocked + version-bump in PR + worktree cleanup safety with 3 guards. (a) A required CI check scans .test-index for unresolved RED markers and blocks session-to-main merge if any are present; named under an umbrella job for stable branch-protection. (b) merge-to-main-pr.sh commits the version-bump on the source branch's HEAD before merge; the S5 story includes the explicit design decision (bump-before-final-review vs. bump-after-final-review-accepting-re-review-dismissal) documented in the ticket. (c) claude-safe (in agent-batch-lifecycle.sh) and harvest-worktree.sh refuse to remove a worktree when ANY of: (i) the branch has an open PR with CI in flight; (ii) the worktree has uncommitted or unpushed changes; (iii) the branch is in a protected list (main, master, develop, release/*). --force bypass prints which guard fired and the PR URL when applicable. The open-PR check uses a 3-tier fallback chain: (1) gh pr list --head <branch>, (2) gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/pulls, (3) for fork PRs missed by both, gh pr list --search 'head:<branch>' or equivalent. S1's spike validates the tier-2 reliability for pre-merge session-branch SHAs; if it fails, tier-3 is promoted. Verification: (a) attempted RED-marker push to main is blocked; (b) sub-PR commit history shows version-bump on source branch; (c) cleanup-against-open-PR test refuses without --force and names which guard fired.

- SC5 — Epic execution discipline — verifiable from commit history. (a) The first story (S1) is a hard blocker for S2-S7 AND its Definition of Done requires: (i) a manual dso:code-reviewer-standard (opus) review of S1's own sub-PR with reviewer-findings.json attached and zero unresolved critical/important findings; (ii) two spike outcomes documented in the S1 ticket comment — the branches: filter base-ref semantics confirmed by a minimal test workflow, AND the SHA-based PR lookup reliability for non-default-branch commits confirmed (or the 3rd-tier fallback promoted). (b) All stories use /dso:sprint orchestration only — no /dso:fix-bug invocations. (c) Modifications are additive in the behavior-preservation sense: existing CI/review workflows and scripts may NOT be deleted; pull_request branch filters MAY be extended to additional base refs (broadening, not narrowing); existing inline gating may have provenance-aware skip paths added INSIDE (preserving original main-base coverage). Verification: epic-close audit confirms all three sub-conditions with an explicit files-touched + behavior-preservation-rule-applied checklist attached to the epic-close comment.
None blocking. Depends on b575's cycle ledger (already merged via PR #232).
Blocked by this epic (unblocked on merge): cf7b-86a9, f27a-3c6a, fb32-215c.

Option E (synthesized from prior-art research): additive new .github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml fires at sub-PR boundary; cycle ledger + DefenseStore re-keyed by (pr_number, commit_sha); integration review at session-to-main reuses verify-session-provenance.sh (exit 0 → skip; exit 1/2 → full-diff fallback); runner-level large-diff fallback uses .gitattributes linguist pre-filter + file-level chunking extending Strategy E + LLM aggregation pass + visibility trailer + OVER_BOUND hard bound; SC3 audit extends base=main filters additively or installs an always-runs umbrella job; SC4 adds RED-test-blocker required check + version-bump on source branch + 3-guard worktree cleanup; SC5 enforces behavior-preservation additive constraint, S1 spike outcomes, and manual opus review on S1.

14 surviving scenarios from red+blue team analysis. Critical: provenance skip swallows un-reviewed amend commits on session branch (mitigation: detect amend chains in verify-session-provenance.sh or caller); file-level chunking cross-file blind spots (accepted operational constraint; aggregation pass partial mitigation). High: cycle ledger force-push reset; FP-recovery escape-hatch erosion (mitigated via OVER_BOUND status); ignore.glob hand-written-code exclusion (mitigated via visibility trailer); required-check rollout (mitigation: stage as non-required first + touch-pr.sh helper); version-bump SHA drift (S4(b) design decision); verify-session-provenance.sh exit-code contract drift (contract test in SC1); non-trailer commits in session branch (fallback to full-diff); per-file context loss (accepted limitation); S1 self-review meaningfulness (partial: SC5(a) DoD + spike). Medium: concurrent ledger writes race (atomic CAS); open-PR-guard race with Jira sync (TOCTOU re-check); audit transition double-runs (one-time allow-list); max_files=0 silent disable (resolved via non-zero validation); test re-run semantics (resolved via latest-run rule). Cross-epic coordination signals are informational only per user direction — this epic blocks all others.
Informational per user direction (this epic has unilateral blocking authority over open epics):
- 1624-5fb9 (P0 bug, ci/llm-review integration-scope short-circuit — superseded by SC1)
- 576b-a6c7, b1a7-20bf (P0 bugs, scope regression from story 20d7 — covered by SC1 + SC5(c))
- a5a9-969b (P0 bug, claude-safe deletes active PRs — covered by SC4(c))
- swap-maple-flyby, heat-dwarf-bone (P0 BLOCKING, Cycle-end arbiter + workflow unification — coordinate trailer-vs-provenance contract)
- solid-wick-dryad, knotty-movie-game (P0 duplicate pair, workflow-config PR flag — feeds SC1 discriminator)
- acrid-lath-elbow (P0, re-review 29 PRs without LLM dispatch — downstream cleanup once SC1 lands)
- 70f6-05f1 / jira-dig-2316 (parallel-worktree-review with Clash — adapts to us)
- 6068-cb2d (completion verifier goal-backward verification — coordinate DSO-Story-Merge trailer contract)
- 53ef-d6fd (PR ownership / Session-Id trailer — coordinate trailer ordering)
- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration — completion-verifier output section ordering)
- dso-8l5h (code-reviewer agent extraction — coordinate bootstrap AC)

- Bright-line conditions that fired: novel architectural pattern (per-sub-PR + provenance-aware skip), performance/scalability (chunked oversized-PR fallback), migration/compatibility (audit base=main gating)
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 20 of 20 (fail-open policy; 6 folded into SC refinements, 14 remain as documented operational risks)

- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): triggered — cycles: 1, gap: technical_feasibility=3 + integration_risk=2 on initial review; resolved via spec refinements (Signal 1 base-ref clarification, Signal 5 chunking scope, Signal 7 3-tier fallback + S1 spike, Signal 8 latest-run semantics, Signal 9 v1.1.0-to-v1.2.0 migration contract); re-review scored technical_feasibility=4, integration_risk=4
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered (no SKILL.md / agent / prompt-template / hook modifications in spec)
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable (no volume-sensitive decision in spec)

- Scope right_sized override: user-direction override applied — Scope reviewer scored right_sized=3 recommending split into review-pipeline + merge-pipeline-integrity epics; user explicitly chose single-epic structure per "EPIC BLOCKS ALL OTHERS" direction recorded in state file 2026-05-19; other Scope dimensions (no_overlap=4, dependency_aware=5, consumer_completeness=5) PASS

justification: "Release script will be updated to account for any new packages or workflows introduced by this epic (per brainstorm Step 3 release-infrastructure check 3dc2-ad99). Verification is via inspection of release.sh diff during the epic close audit."
